states.why: The room is lit from the first note: a low blue on all four lamps. Nothing switches on later; things get brighter.
Bars 4-6: the blue bed comes up a step where the score marks the build.
Bars 7-10: a steady blue bed. The rhythm here is the brass, and the amber flashes carry it -- the bed does not pulse against them.
Bars 11-14: the inner pair holds blue under the voice alone; the outer pair grows with the singer's line.
Bars 19-22: a steady blue floor under the second phrase of the riff, so the glares and chases rise out of a lit room and fall back into one.
The last bar before the drop, same floor.

From the downbeat of the drop: a red core in a blue frame -- drive's two pairs call and respond, inner red, outer blue, flipping on the beat. The first red the room has seen. (Split from the state that straddled 49.75, whose first bar was sitting on the dim build bed.) Floor 0.72 so the frame is brighter than the build it answers.
Bars 24-25: the drop keeps arriving. Red and blue trade bars on a high floor.

Bars 26-28: the bass drops out and the singer leads. The room turns blue and the pairs swap at half speed -- the same drive, but wider and calmer, so the singer has the floor. Red comes back only as the runs on beat 4.
Bar 29: bass and drums return, hardest in the section. Red home again, floor higher than the arrival, straight into the bar-30 acceleration.
Bar 30: the drums stop, so the drive stops with them. A plain blue floor under the white climb; the drive comes back with the impact.
Drop 2 (from the impact at 65.75): red home, blue kicks, high floor -- stopping two beats before the exchange so the room can ease down into it.
The exchange: a blue bed under the two singers. Their lines are drawn on top as slow swells anchored to where each phrase starts in the score -- nothing here follows the microphone live.
Bars 39-43, drop 3: red home, blue kicks, the highest floor of the three drops.
Bar 45: a plain blue floor under the white climb into the resolve.
The resolve: the brightest bed in the show under the colour wave.

The loudest twelve seconds on the record: the two pairs call and respond on EVERY beat, red and WHITE. White is a hit, and here the song hits on every beat, so the row does -- which makes this both the brightest and the busiest stretch of the show, where it belongs. The head is white with the prism; the four hardest kicks get a white strobe on top.
The come-down: amber, the orchestra's colour from bars 7-10, comes back as the room's colour. It does not pulse; the strings' own swells are drawn on top.
113.0: the score marks a pause and the band is at 3%. The room dips with it for half a second.
The strings return; the amber bed with them.
The last entrance: amber settles a step.
The beat has gone; the room settles again.
The song ends in silence; the room fades to black over two and a half seconds with it.

gestures.why: The head is a still white pin on the left wall, low, for the whole opening. It does not move. Its first movement will be an event because of these fourteen seconds.
First vocal phrase (1.76-8.49 in the score): the inner pair lifts slowly through the line, a quarter above the bed at the start, half above it at the end.
Two beats before the entrance the whole row starts to swell white, from the bed's level to full, so the hit on 13.83 is the top of a rise the room has already begun.
The head leaves its first spot one beat before the entrance, so it ARRIVES at the new one on 13.83 rather than starting to move there.
The entrance at 13.83: one white beat at the top of the swell, then a 600ms fall back to the bed.
Third vocal phrase (15.90-17.22): the inner pair lifts again, leading into the tempo change at 17.75.

Bar 7: the horns punch just before beat 2. Amber on the outer pair for one beat -- amber belongs to the brass, and this is the first time it is heard. The inner pair stays on the blue pulse, so the room reads blue with a brass flash on each side.
Bar 8: the same punch, a little heavier, so a little brighter.
Bar 9: the horns stop punching and climb instead, rising through the bar into bar 10. The outer pair swells amber with them.
Bar 10: timpani and violins swell for the last beat and a half. The whole row swells amber into the hit.
Towards the riff the pin dims, so the black at 32.72 is arrived at rather than cut to, and the white hit at 33.75 lands in a room that had been going quiet.
The hit at 25.56, where the song changes section: full amber for two beats, then amber is gone until the outro, where the orchestra takes over again and it comes back as a callback.
The lead-in phrase (27.02-33.75 in the score): the outer pair grows with the singer for six seconds, from just above the bed to two thirds.
Two beats before the riff, over the pause the score marks at 33.0, the row swells white.
One beat of nothing before the riff lands.

THE BASS RIFF. Bass and strings, no drums, no voice: the one fixture that can point becomes the soloist. Clean white beam, no prism, snapping to a new wall on every downbeat -- four bars, four places -- and drifting across each bar with the bass. The row stays a dim blue field underneath so the beam cuts. Now: it NODS hard and FLASHES on beats 2 and 2-and-a-half, where the riff punches, from the very first bar -- and each turn to a new wall begins a beat early so the head arrives on the downbeat instead of leaving on it.

33.75s: bass and strings arrive together out of a one-second black. ONE beat of the whole row in white -- the row's single big statement in this phrase -- and then it drops to the blue bed and the head takes over. This was the biggest arrival in the first half of the song and it had been getting a dim bed fading in.

Bar 15: the red spark leaves on beat 2 and ARRIVES on the 'and' of 2 -- which is where this riff actually punches, every bar. A run is read when it lands, not when it starts, so it is aimed to land on the hit and takes a quarter of a second, not a whole beat. Left to right.

Bar 18: the borrowed major turns MINOR at 40.0s. One beat of the whole row lifting in blue-violet on the downbeat, the first time the row has spoken at full since the riff began. The head snaps at the same instant.
Bar 18: under the blue turn and the last spark a red glow grows across the row, so the two join steps at 41.02 and 41.30 rise out of red and the other pair is never black behind them.

Bar 18: the red spark leaves on beat 2 and ARRIVES on the 'and' of 2 -- which is where this riff actually punches, every bar. A run is read when it lands, not when it starts, so it is aimed to land on the hit and takes a quarter of a second, not a whole beat. Right to left.

The joining piece. After the riff's first phrase the song walks down through two quick chords: F at 41.02, E at 41.30, landing on D minor at 41.76 where the second phrase starts. Step one: the outer pair, red.
Step two: the inner pair, red. The two steps close inwards, and the full blue glare of the second phrase lands on 41.76.

Second phrase, drums creeping in: the head keeps its stations but now STROBES on every downbeat -- the first strobe of the show, white, a burst at the top of each bar. Rhythm from the fixture that can do it. Now: it NODS hard and FLASHES on beats 2 and 2-and-a-half, where the riff punches, from the very first bar -- and each turn to a new wall begins a beat early so the head arrives on the downbeat instead of leaving on it.

Bar 19, beats 1-2: the whole row BLAZES for two beats Blue, not violet: the second phrase had drifted to purple and lost the red entirely, so the half that was meant to escalate went from three colours to one dim one. The bed stays blue; the red grows in what moves.

Beat 3: the row collapses to ONE lamp running right to left in a single beat, everything else dark. In RED -- the spark's colour. In phrase one the red was a quarter-second spark once a bar; here it is a whole running lamp, twice a bar. Same identity, more of it.

Beat 4: and straight back the other way. In RED -- the spark's colour. In phrase one the red was a quarter-second spark once a bar; here it is a whole running lamp, twice a bar. Same identity, more of it.

Bar 22: the row holds blue and swells for three beats, right up to the single black beat.
One beat of nothing before the drop. The music is at full weight here, so two beats read as a fault; one reads as a breath.
49.75s, THE DROP. Every lamp to full WHITE for one beat, snapped, no fade. The room has been blue for fifty seconds; this is the first white and the drums arriving.
Bars 23-25: red prism, snapping side to side every two beats, a nod on every beat.
52.76s: the whole band at full strength, six families at once. One full BEAT of white across the row, held, not an 80ms flash -- the head keeps snapping red underneath it.
Bar 26, beat 1: one white beat marks the singer's entrance and the change of room.
Bars 26-28: the head stands still in the centre, white, and nods on beats 1 and 3 with the singer. No prism, no strobe -- it is listening.
Bar 26, beat 4: a fast red run across the blue room, the pickup into the next bar -- the lights answering the singer's line.
Bar 27, beat 4: a fast red run across the blue room, the pickup into the next bar -- the lights answering the singer's line.
Bar 28, beat 4: a fast red run across the blue room, the pickup into the next bar -- the lights answering the singer's line. The third one runs straight into bar 29.
Bar 29, beat 1: one white beat as the bass and drums come back.
Bar 29: red prism is back, now with a strobe on every beat, for the hardest bar before the pause.
The head joins the acceleration: dead centre, white, no prism, strobing on every beat -- the first time the head has flashed white since the riff. Then the beat of black at 65.25, then red.
Bar 30: the row goes white and climbs for three beats -- from the drive's level to full, no flicker -- while the head strobes on the beat. Then one black beat, then the impact of drop 2.
One beat of nothing before the drums come back full at bar 31.
Bar 31 lands. The build was kept cold on purpose so this is the first white the room sees.

Drop 2: the head does what it does in every drop -- red prism, snapping side to side every two beats, a nod and a strobe pop on each beat. The same move in every drop is what makes them read as the same show.
The head comes to rest in the centre, white, low, two beats before the exchange begins, and stays there for the whole conversation.
The last two beats of drop 2: the row turns blue and eases down to the exchange's level, so the quiet section is arrived at, not cut to.
Lead singer, phrase one (73.75-79.51 in the score): the inner pair, blue, lifting slowly through the line.
The answering voice (74.00-75.26): the outer pair, red, for as long as it sings.
Lead singer, phrase two (80.50-81.76): the whole row rises blue into drop 3's first bar.
Drop 3 (bars 39-43): the drop head, from the section's first bar.
Bars 39-40: two beats of white rising into the black beat before drop 3.
One beat of nothing before bar 40, the hardest span in the song.
Bar 40 lands. The build was kept cold on purpose so this is the first white the room sees.
the drums arrive at 85.76s
Bar 45: the same climb into the resolve. Three beats of white rising, one black beat, the impact.
One beat of nothing before the resolve at 91.76.
THE PEAK at 91.76s — the loudest stretch of the song

THE COLOUR WAVE as this section's identity: the row stays lit in blue and a RED position walks across it, twice a bar, turning each bar. Only the hue moves. Red over blue, not white over red: white is a hit in this show and a white wave here outshone the loudest section that follows. Peak 0.85: this is a RESOLVE, and it sits under the climax that follows, not over it.

The head RESTS through the resolve -- a still red pin, low, no prism -- after eight bars of snapping. Its white explosion at 97.76 is an entrance because of these six bars, and the row's colour wave has the room to itself.

The head goes WHITE for the first time since the build -- prism pulsing, strobing and kicking on every beat, snapping side to side. The biggest the head gets, saved for the biggest the song gets.
A WHITE STROBE OVER A RED HOLD on one of the four hardest kicks in the song (98.50s): every 'on' is white and every 'off' is red, so the flash has a colour. Two beats.
White strobe for three beats, right up to the single black beat before the loudest kick.
One beat of nothing before the loudest kick in the song.

THE LOUDEST KICK IN THE SONG at 102.76s -- full strength in the kick lane, the top of four consecutive bars that hold the four hardest hits on the record. Whole rig, full white, held for three beats. This is the peak of the show and it is placed on the hit rather than on a bar line. Four beats: this is the loudest kick in the song and the show's brightest moment lives here, not in the build.
The head rests in amber, still, through the strip-back.
The breakdown at 109.76: the room turns amber at the drive's level and falls over four beats to the come-down bed. The colour changes on the beat; the brightness comes down as a slope.
The strings enter at 113.75 and swell for six seconds (the score's strings lane goes 0.3 to 0.9); the room swells amber with them, up to the register shift at 120.29.
120.29s, the octave lift: the head's ONE slow sweep of the whole night, amber, across the room and back once a bar, to the end. Saved for the resolution.
The violins climb from 120.3; the room swells white for two and a half seconds into the last entrance.
The last entrance at 123.77 and the song's final peak at 124.5: amber, nearly full, held to where the band drops away at 126.
One beat of nothing where the beat drops away, as the score marks the rhythm change.
